newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-INTER GOALSCORER GANZ FIRED UP FOR UEFA CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INTER GOALSCORER GANZ FIRED UP FOR UEFA CUP.

text.p: Inter Milan's Maurizio Ganz, top scorer in the UEFA Cup this season, believes Wednesday's second leg of the final against Germany's Schalke will be his big date with history.
The 28-year-old striker, who has become a San Siro crowd favourite after scoring eight times in the cup, is one of the venerable Milan club's few players never to have won an international trophy.
Some, such as defender Giuseppe Bergomi in his 17th season at Inter, have won the UEFA Cup twice.
This year, Ganz, who has been overlooked by the Italian national team, feels it carries his name.
"It's my big opportunity, my date with history," said Ganz. "If we fail, all my goals will have been in vain."
Inter, third in the Italian league, have won the UEFA Cup twice in the past decade -- in 1991 and 1994 -- and must be fancied to overturn the 1-0 deficit from the away leg.
But it will be the first time in this season's competition that they play a second leg having to make up ground. Their opponents have scored away in every round so far.
If Inter do win in Milan, it will be hailed more as the start of a new cycle than completion of a hat-trick.

For one thing, it would be the first trophy the Milan club have seen under the leadership of ambitious president Massimo Moratti, who took over the club in February 1995 and has invested a fortune in rebuilding the squad.
While Schalke have to win the cup to qualify for Europe next season, Inter have no such worries.

They are already guaranteed at least a UEFA Cup place next season but still have their eyes on the second European Cup slot as runners-up behind Juventus, who are expected to clinch the title against Ganz's old club Atalanta on Friday.
But that does not mean the pressure is off.

Moratti wants a return for his money, English coach Roy Hodgson -- joining Blackburn in England next season -- wants to leave with a lasting achievement and the players themselves need something to stave off the sense of a squandered season.

The problem for Inter, who return to full strength after missing French attacking midfielder Youri Djorkaeff, compatriot Jocelyn Angloma and England's Paul Ince through suspension, is that they have flattered to deceive.

"It's true that throughout the season we have regularly failed when faced with moments of truth," said 30-year-old former Italy goalkeeper Gianluca Pagliuca, who helped Sampdoria win the European Cup Winners' Cup in 1990 and the Italian league in 1991.
"But there is always a first time in life. Against Schalke, for the first time, Inter will not flunk the test.

"We absolutely want to win this cup. We feel we have a moral obligation to the fans and the club. Winning the UEFA Cup will give a purpose to the season and maybe give us the impetus to win the last two matches remaining in the league."
Inter drew 1-1 with Roma on Sunday, a result that showed many players had their thoughts elsewhere.
"There was something on the players' minds that stopped them being aggressive and sharp," Hodgson said. "I think you'll see an entirely different Inter against Schalke."
Schalke also have a near first-choice line-up having rested a number of key players in Saturday's 2-1 defeat at 1860 Munich in which Martin Max scored on his return from injury.
Veteran 31-year-old libero Olaf Thon, nursing a thigh strain, will play, hoping to make up for past disappointments.
"I lost three times in European semifinals with Bayern Munich," the former German international said. "Now I want to win the UEFA Cup. If I do it with Schalke it will be a sensation."
Dutch striker Youri Mulder (torn ligaments) and U.S. midfielder Tom Dooley (thigh strain) are out.

The club have not won for 10 league games and have scored just three goals in the process. "If we make the same mistakes against Inter we needn't bother turning up in Milan," coach Huub Stevens said after Saturday's defeat.
But manager Rudi Assauer was more understanding.
"For us, it's all or nothing on Wednesday. That's why, after a tough season, we needed to let ourselves recover."
Probable teams:
Inter - Gianluca Pagliuca; Jocelyn Angloma, Alessandro Pistone, Salvatore Fresi, Massimo Paganin, Ciriaco Sforza, Paul Ince, Javier Zanetti, Youri Djorkaeff, Ivan Zamorano, Maurizio Ganz.
Schalke - Jens Lehmann, Olaf Thon, Thomas Linke, Johan de Kock, Yves Eigenrauch, Radoslav Latal, Jiri Nemec, Andreas Mueller, Mike Bueskens, Marc Wilmots, Martin Max.
